newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Peacekeepers unearth Liberia arms cache.
newsitem.headline: Peacekeepers unearth Liberia arms cache.

text.p: West African peacekeepers have unearthed a large arms cache in Liberia in a swamp near Bong Mines and made dozens of arrests, their commander said on Wednesday.

General Victor Malu told reporters the swoop, which netted the biggest arms find since the end of disarmament in early February, took place on Tuesday in the abandoned mining town 50 miles (80 km) north west of the capital Monrovia.

"The message was clear to all former factions that those found with arms after the January 31 deadline are purely considered and treated as criminals," the head of the Nigerian-led ECOMOG peacekeeping force said.
The peacekeepers extended the deadline into early February in remote upcountry areas.
The arms cache found on Tuesday included AK-47 automatic rifles and rocket-propelled grenades.

Liberia, founded by freed American slaves in 1847, holds presidential and legislative elections on May 30 to end seven years of civil war under a peace plan brokered by its West African neighbours. The war killed well over 150,000 people.
